nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a connected open set and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on $U$. If the conjugate function $z \mapsto \overline{f(z)}$ is also holomorphic on $U$, then $f$ is constant on $U$: there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = c$ for all $z \in U$.
nodes.title: A holomorphic function with holomorphic conjugate is constant

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be the function $f(z) = \bar z$. Then $f$ is not complex-differentiable at any point $z \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Complex conjugation is nowhere complex-differentiable
